subject: Intro request — short peer sync for latency-sensitive fintech (EU)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Henriksen <eva.h@norbank.no>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Quick ask — 20–30m peer sync for an EU fintech evaluation (StarLend)

Hi Eva —

Hope you’re well. I’m working StarLend (late-stage fintech, payments/fraud use case) on a tight procurement timeline — they’ve asked for a short peer call with an active Redwood customer in Europe who uses us for low-latency inference in production.

High-level: StarLend wants to validate 99th percentile latency, regional data residency, and how you handle bursty traffic around peak transaction windows. They’re specifically interested in batching/kv-cache patterns and any lessons learned about tail latency.

Would you be willing to jump on a 20–30 minute call this week or next to speak candidly about your deployment? We’d keep it high-level (no NDAs required) and I can share a brief agenda up front.

Prefer windows: Wed 18:30–20:00 CEST or Thu 08:00–10:00 CEST, but we’ll work around your schedule.

I’m attaching a one-page use-case brief to help frame the conversation. If you’re open, I can introduce you to the StarLend procurement contact (Oliver) and propose times.

Huge appreciate — and totally fine if you want to loop in a platform/infra colleague.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: starLend-usecase-brief.pdf (1 page PDF — brief on fraud detection / expected throughput)
From: Eva Henriksen <eva.h@norbank.no>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver@starlend.com>
Cc: NorBank-Infra <infra@norbank.no>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 20–30m peer sync for an EU fintech evaluation (StarLend)

Hi Jasmine,

Happy to help — glad to hear StarLend is evaluating this carefully. We’ve been running Redwood in production for ~18 months (in eu-central with customer-managed keys) and have a short list of practical points we can cover:
- How we configured batching and KV cache to protect tail latency
- Typical throughput and 99p numbers during peak windows
- Our roll-forward / rollback practices and incident examples (brief)

I can do Thu 19 May 09:00–09:30 CEST or Fri 20 May 14:00–14:30 CEST. I’ll attach a quick deployment sketch that shows our placement and network path.

Cc’d infra to make sure a technical person can join if needed. Looking forward to a short, practical chat.

Regards,
Eva Henriksen
Head of ML Platforms, NorBank
eva.h@norbank.no

Attachment: norbank-deployment-sketch.png (PNG — architecture sketch)
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@starlend.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Eva Henriksen <eva.h@norbank.no>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 12:27:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 20–30m peer sync for an EU fintech evaluation (StarLend)

Thanks Jasmine & Eva — really appreciate you making time. Either of the proposed slots works for our procurement and platform leads; Thu 19 May 09:00 CEST is ideal.

A couple quick asks for the call agenda so we can prep:
- 5 min intros and one-line description of what NorBank uses Redwood for
- 10–12 min technical: 99p latency, batching strategies, autoscaling/burst handling
- 5–8 min procurement/Q&A: data residency, contractual SLAs, and any compliance artifacts you can reference (SOC2, audit logs)

Also: do you have any customer-facing artifacts (short case blurb or a one-pager) we can use on our side? If you prefer, we can run the call with an NDA but we’d prefer not to if it can be avoided.

Oliver Grant
Head of Infrastructure, StarLend
oliver@starlend.com | +44 20 7946 0421
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Quick ask — short prep + materials for StarLend intro call

Looping Marcus in — he’ll bring the 99p latency numbers and a concise troubleshooting slide (we’ll keep it one slide). Marcus, please prepare:
- 99p and p95 numbers for eu-central across our typical batching configs
- A short note on KV cache behavior and recommended thresholds for StarLend’s expected token/sequence distributions
- One-sentence summary of fallback policies (model variants/region routing) we can share publicly

Jasmine — I’ll draft a 1-pager you can share directly with Oliver (public-friendly). Marcus — attach the numbers and a one-slide PNG by EOD Thu so we can send it ahead of the call.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
